profile.summary: DNALONGBENCH is five DNA prediction tasks that need long input sequences, up to about 1 million base pairs: enhancer-target gene pairs, eQTLs, 3D chromatin contact maps, regulatory sequence activity and base-pair transcription initiation signals. Each task compares a task-specific expert model, a CNN and fine-tuned DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS). It is for developers testing whether long-context DNA models capture long-range dependencies.

summary_quotes.text: we introduce DNALONGBENCH, a benchmark dataset covering five key genomics tasks with long-range dependencies up to 1 million base pairs: enhancer-target gene interaction, expression quantitative trait loci, 3D genome organization, regulatory sequence activity, and transcription initiation signals.
We assess DNALONGBENCH using five methods: a task-specific expert model, a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based model, and three fine-tuned DNA foundation models

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether a model can use long DNA context for problems where distant sequence matters: linking enhancers to target genes, flagging eQTLs, predicting chromatin contacts, predicting thousands of epigenomic tracks, and predicting transcription initiation at base-pair resolution.

quotes.text: we introduce DNALONGBENCH, a benchmark dataset covering five key genomics tasks with long-range dependencies up to 1 million base pairs: enhancer-target gene interaction, expression quantitative trait loci, 3D genome organization, regulatory sequence activity, and transcription initiation signals.

sections.title: Enhancer-target gene and eQTL tasks
sections.body: Enhancer-target gene pairs are CRISPRi-validated enhancer-promoter interactions in K562 cells from three studies, kept within 450 kb of the TSS; 2,602 samples, scored by AUROC. The eQTL task adapts Enformer's SuSiE fine-mapped eQTL set for the top nine tissues, keeps candidates within 450 kb of the TSS, masks other variants in each interval, and splits 8:1:1 by stratified random sampling; 31,282 samples, scored by AUROC.

For this study, we selected the top nine tissues based on the number of variants.

To reduce bias caused by putative eQTLs within the interval between an eQTL candidate and the gene promoter pair, we masked the sequences of all variants within each variant-promoter pair. sections.title: Contact map, regulatory activity and transcription initiation tasks
sections.body: Contact maps use Akita's processed data for five cell lines plus four more from the 4DN portal, 1 Mbp inputs at 2 kb bins, split by random virtual contigs 8:1:1 into 7008, 419 and 413 sequences, scored by SCC and PCC. Regulatory activity uses Enformer's 5313 human and 1643 mouse tracks, with 1937 human and 2017 mouse test sequences, scored by PCC averaged over test samples. Transcription initiation uses Puffin's data for five assays on both strands, evaluated on test chromosomes 8 and 9 by PCC.

quotes.text: We used the processed data from Akita
which includes chromatin interaction data from five cell lines: HFF, H1-hESC, GM12878, IMR-90, and HCT116.

The human genome was divided into non-overlapping virtual contigs and randomly assigned to training, validation, and testing sets with an 8:1:1 ratio. The dataset contains 7008 training sequences, 419 validation sequences, and 413 test sequences. Model performance on the held-out test set was evaluated using the stratum-adjusted correlation coefficient (SCC) and the Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC).
For this task, we compiled human and mouse genomic tracks from the Enformer paper
The target labels consist of 5313 human tracks and 1643 mouse tracks measuring epigenomic marks.

For the human genome, the data is split into 34,021 training, 2213 validation, and 1937 test sequences. For the mouse genome, the dataset is split into 29,295 training, 2209 validation, and 2017 test sequences.
Specifically, the Pearson correlation coefficients were computed for each sample across all positions and tracks, and the mean was taken across all samples in the test set.
Specifically, the task predicts transcription initiation signals on both strands for five experimental techniques: FANTOM CAGE, ENCODE CAGE, ENCODE RAMPAGE, GRO-cap, and PRO-cap
We used processed labeled data from the Puffin model
Predictions were generated for entire test chromosomes (chr8 and chr9) using a sliding window with a step size of 50 kb, with the center 50 kb of each 100 kb prediction being evaluated.

Each input sequence, spanning 1 million base pairs (Mbp), is divided into 512 genomic bins at a resolution of 2 kb per bin.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Models are trained or fine-tuned on each task's training split and scored on its test set with the task's metric: AUROC for the two classification tasks, SCC and PCC for contact maps, PCC for the two regression tasks. Foundation models feed sequence features to linear heads; for eQTL, reference and alternate representations are combined before a classifier. The paper reports that expert models scored highest on every task.

quotes.text: For the remaining tasks, we fed the DNA sequences into the DNA foundation model to obtain feature vectors, then applied linear layers to predict logits at different resolutions.

For the eQTL task, we extracted last-layer hidden representations from both the reference and allele sequences, averaged and concatenated them, and applied a binary classification layer to predict whether the variant was positive.

We filtered this data by retaining enhancer-promoter pair candidates within 450 kb of the gene transcription start site (TSS) and applied additional filtering criteria. Model performance was evaluated using AUROC.

The human genome was divided into non-overlapping virtual contigs and randomly assigned to training, validation, and testing sets with an 8:1:1 ratio. The dataset contains 7008 training sequences, 419 validation sequences, and 413 test sequences. Model performance on the held-out test set was evaluated using the stratum-adjusted correlation coefficient (SCC) and the Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC).
The benchmarking results consistently showed that expert models achieved the highest scores across all tasks.

sections.body: Create the conda environment, clone the repository and install the package, download a task's data from Dataverse, then run the CNN baseline's train.py for that task; the script trains, saves the best validation checkpoint to best_model.pt, and prints the test metric for the final-epoch model, not the saved checkpoint.

steps.title: Create environment and install
steps.shell:
conda create -n dnalongbench python=3.9 -y

steps.title: Train and test the CNN on enhancer-target gene prediction
steps.shell:
cd experiments/CNN
python train.py \
    --task_name enhancer_target_gene_prediction \
    --root ./data \
    --save_dir ./results/ETGP \
    --subset None \
    --batch_size 2
steps.explanation: The CNN README's command for ETGP, run from experiments/CNN where train.py sits. It trains for --num_epochs epochs (default 5), saves the weights of the best validation epoch to best_model.pt, and then scores the test set with the model as it is after the final epoch; the script never reloads best_model.pt.
